Trial9 (block-Jacobi convergence BREAKTHROUGH + cost analysis, HEAD unchanged=baseline-equiv). FIXED block Jacobi convergence: the stall (offfrac 0.41) was eigh-sorting column THRASHING -- eigh sorts the 2bs pair eigenvalues, permuting columns across the p|q block boundary every round. FIX: assign each eigenvector column to the p or q half where it has max weight (argsort of sum(Rv[:bs]^2)-sum(Rv[bs:]^2), split at bs) -> block partition stays stable -> CONVERGES: offfrac 3.3e-2@sweep2, 4.5e-4@sweep5 (gate 1.2e-2), ~4 sweeps. TF32 rotations are CHEAP (40ms total for B=640). BUT block-eigh GENERATION dominates: 2560 stacked 128x128 eighs/round (cuSOLVER 35ms, megakernel 62ms slower) x28 rounds = 980ms. Full block-Jacobi PyTorch: bs=64 sw=4 = 495-623ms vs cuSOLVER 172ms (3.6x slower); bs=32 doesn't converge in 4 sweeps. Bottleneck is per-round small-eigh launch overhead + generation, NOT rotations. Scalar Jacobi converges in 6 sweeps but is bandwidth-bound (~1s global-mem at n=512, M=1MB doesn't fit 228KB SMEM). PATH TO WIN: fused CUDA block-Jacobi kernel (one CTA/matrix, 128x128 pair in SMEM=64KB fits, in-kernel pair-eigh + global block-col rotation) to kill the launch overhead -- est 10-30ms could beat cuSOLVER 172ms. Trial10 (fused block-Jacobi CUDA kernel built & measured; HEAD unchanged=baseline-equiv 48084us). Wrote a fused block-Jacobi eigh kernel (one CTA/matrix, 128x128 pair block in SMEM=128KB, in-SMEM scalar-Jacobi rotation generator + weight-based column reassignment to keep block partition stable, global block-col/row rotation apply + V accumulation). CORRECTNESS CONFIRMED at B=8..640: 4 sweeps -> M offfrac 5.5e-3, eigen resid 7.4e-3, orth 1.5e-3 -- ALL THREE GATES PASS (gates 1.2e-2/1.2e-2/6.1e-3). But SPEED: 24 SECONDS at B=640 (140x slower than cuSOLVER 172ms). Root cause: the in-SMEM rotation-generator (diagonalizing each 128x128 pair) is fully serial -- inner=6 sweeps x 128*127/2 rotations x per-rotation __syncthreads x 112 pair-diags/matrix = ~5.4M syncs/matrix serial, + single-thread perm selection-sort. CONCLUSIVE: block Jacobi CONVERGES (gates pass in 4 sweeps) and its rotations are cheap (14ms block-col GEMM / 40ms dense), but GENERATING the rotations (diagonalizing the 128x128 pairs) costs ~1s (cuSOLVER stacked 980ms, in-kernel 24s) -- it is the SAME eigh problem recursively at smaller scale, so block Jacobi cannot escape the inner-eigh cost. Combined with the bandwidth-bound scalar Jacobi (~1s, M=1MB doesn't fit SMEM at n=512) and the PD-shift rank-collapse artifact, the dense n=512 full-spectrum shapes do not yield to any subspace/Jacobi GEMM approach. Keeping HEAD at baseline-equivalent no-regression.

KEY: reflectors on one column are independent of other columns, so one thread owns a whole column across ALL reflectors -> NO inter-reflector barrier, V in fast SMEM. V doesn't fit SMEM at medium n, so process V in column-blocks (BV cols) in the post-reduction free SMEM A region; global V traffic 2*n^3 -> ~2*n^2*(n/BV). Shape2 n=352: 17509->15200us (now 1.32x vs cuSOLVER baseline 20111). Geomean 47392->46669us. n=448 0.91x->0.99x. Validated 39/39, 0 fallbacks. Route cap 400.
